record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Motion of simple bodies in Newtonian aerodynamics
record.original_question: In planar Newtonian aerodynamics, let B be a compact body with piecewise smooth boundary and uniformly distributed mass, moving in a medium of resting point particles that reflect elastically from the boundary. When B has a simple non-disc shape such as an ellipse, a triangle, or the rod [-1,1] × {0}, describe the motion of B for all t ≥ 0.

evidence.quote: Problem: Suppose that B has a simple shape: an ellipse, a triangle, a rod B = [−1, 1]×{0}, etc. (The trivial case when the body is a disc is excluded.) Describe the motion of B for t ≥ 0.

artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature treats the case of a rough disc and various optimization of mean resistance problems, but no published work appears to give a complete description of the motion of a non-disc simple body (ellipse, triangle, or rod) in a resting medium with elastic reflections. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Motion of a rough disc in Newtonian aerodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the two-dimensional motion of a rough disc in a zero-temperature medium with elastic reflections.
status_evidence.claim: Available results address the disc case; non-disc simple bodies are not covered.

status_evidence.title: Spinning rough disc moving in a rarefied medium
status_evidence.snippet: Considers spinning rough disc in a rarefied medium with elastic reflections.
status_evidence.claim: Further work focuses on discs rather than ellipses, triangles, or rods.
